RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

The panel's composition is, by itself, evidence of nothing. All-female panels are common in laboratory medicine and nursing-adjacent fields, and research doesn't show that same-sex panels reliably favour their own sex. Raising it would read as an accusation you can't support, and it tends to discredit the legitimate parts of your case.

Those parts are real: you hold a higher research qualification, and "broad leadership experience" is vague enough to deserve scrutiny. But a department-head role weights management over research depth, and her management course plus that experience is a defensible fit.

Pursue the written explanation instead — in writing, to HR, citing your earlier request and any statutory deadline. Judge the decision on what the reasons say.
